name: Stored drinking water
spec: Commercially bottled, or tap water in food-grade containers rotated every 6 months
notes: One gallon per person per day is the federal planning figure. It covers drinking and minimal hygiene, not bathing or laundry.

name: Rigid water container
spec: 7-gallon food-grade HDPE with a spigot

name: Hollow-fibre water filter
spec: 0.1-micron absolute hollow-fibre, gravity or squeeze feed
notes: Removes bacteria and protozoa. Does not remove viruses. See the filtration skill.

name: Unscented household bleach
spec: Sodium hypochlorite 5-9%, no added scent, no splash-less or gel formulations
notes: Loses potency. Replace annually. Scented, splash-less and gel bleaches are not safe for water treatment.

name: Stainless steel pot with lid
spec: 4-quart, flat-bottomed, lid included
notes: The lid matters. Boiling uncovered wastes fuel and water.

name: Shelf-stable food
spec: Ready-to-eat, no cooking or water required, around 2000 kcal per person-day

name: Bulk staple calories
spec: Rice, beans, oats or pasta in sealed buckets with oxygen absorbers
notes: Cheapest calories per dollar by a wide margin, but requires water and heat to cook. Do not build a whole plan on food you cannot cook.

name: Canister stove
spec: Screw-on isobutane canister stove with integrated igniter

name: Stove fuel canister
spec: 230g isobutane/propane mix

name: LED headlamp
spec: Hands-free, red-light mode, runs on common cells
notes: Hands-free matters more than brightness. A bright torch you must hold is worse than a dim lamp you need not.

name: AA batteries
spec: Lithium primary cells for cold tolerance and shelf life

name: USB power bank
spec: 20,000 mAh / ~74 Wh, USB-C power delivery
notes: Self-discharges. Top it up every three months or it will be flat when it matters.

name: NOAA weather radio
spec: Hand-crank or solar, receives NOAA Weather Radio All Hazards

name: Household first aid kit
spec: Trauma dressings, gauze, tape, irrigation syringe, tweezers, gloves, shears

name: Prescription medication buffer
spec: 30-day surplus of each maintenance medication, rotated
notes: The highest-value item in this catalogue for anyone who takes a daily medication, and the one most often forgotten. Arrange it with your prescriber in advance.

name: Twin-bucket emergency toilet
spec: Two 5-gallon buckets, snap-on seat lid, heavy liners, cover material
notes: Sanitation failure is the leading cause of illness in prolonged outages. This is not an optional item.

name: Cover material
spec: Sawdust, wood shavings, peat or dry soil

name: Alcohol hand sanitiser
spec: At least 60% ethanol or 70% isopropanol
notes: Not a substitute for soap and water where those exist, and ineffective against some pathogens.

name: Bar soap
spec: Plain, unscented

name: Multitool
spec: Locking pliers, knife, drivers, file

name: Utility shut-off wrench
spec: Non-sparking four-way gas and water meter key
notes: Stored at the meter, not in a drawer. A tool you cannot find is a tool you do not own.

name: Duct tape
spec: Cloth-backed, 2-inch

name: Paper road map
spec: Current local and regional street atlas
notes: Works with a dead phone and a dead GPS constellation. Mark your rally points on it by hand.

name: Document pouch
spec: Waterproof, with copies of ID, insurance, deeds, prescriptions, bank details

name: Cash in small bills
spec: Mixed ones, fives and tens. Card readers and ATMs fail with the grid
notes: Small denominations. In an outage nobody can make change for a fifty.

name: Wool blanket
spec: Wool or wool blend, insulates when damp

name: Heavy tarp
spec: 10x12 ft, reinforced grommets

name: N95 respirator
spec: NIOSH-approved N95, fit-tested where possible
notes: For wildfire smoke and dust. Does not protect against gases or vapours.

name: Pealess whistle
spec: Pealess, works wet
notes: Carries far further than a voice, and you can blow one for hours. Shouting lasts about ten minutes.

name: Sturdy closed shoes
spec: Broken in, closed toe, usable for walking several miles
notes: Kept at the bedside. Broken glass is the signature injury of a night-time event.
